stories.headline: Somaliland marks first Independence Day following Israeli recognition Somaliland leaders tout stability and strategic importance as a hub, yet recognition from other nations remains elusive.
stories.summary: Somaliland has marked its first Independence Day since Israel formally recognized it as an independent and sovereign state on December 26, 2025. This recognition makes Israel the first country to do so. Somaliland leaders highlighted the region's stability and strategic importance as a hub, emphasizing its potential. Despite this milestone, recognition from other nations remains elusive. The Israeli government's decision has instructed its authorities to address the issue with the United Nations, African Union, Arab League, and other relevant regional entities. Somaliland's leaders continue to push for broader international recognition, citing the region's unique position and stability in the area. The celebration of Independence Day marks a significant step for Somaliland, but the path to widespread recognition is still uncertain.

stories.headline: Hezbollah War Persists Despite Truce Extension Air Defenses Activated in Isfahan for Unknown Reason, Iran's Mehr News Agency Reports. Trump Says He Called Off an Attack on Iran Scheduled for Tuesday at Gulf
stories.summary: Hezbollah and Israel continue to exchange fire despite a truce extension, with Lebanon's death toll exceeding 3,000. The conflict reignited due to the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. US President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire on April 16, but fighting has persisted. Trump also revealed that he called off a planned attack on Iran scheduled for Tuesday at the request of Gulf allies. Meanwhile, Iran has set conditions for a deal, including ending Israel's war in Lebanon. Pakistan has deployed 8,000 troops and military equipment to Saudi Arabia under a secret defence pact. Iran's semi-official Fars news agency reported that the US has set five conditions in response to Tehran's proposal, including limiting Iran's nuclear sites and transferring its enriched uranium stockpile to the US. Air defenses were activated in Isfahan, Iran, for an unknown reason, according to Mehr News Agency.

stories.headline: US says American contracted Ebola in Congo as CDC announces new travel screening measures Health officials to take ‘proactive measures’ in response to the ongoing Ebola virus epidemic in the DRC and Uganda
stories.summary: A US citizen has contracted Ebola after being exposed while working with a medical missionary group in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The individual, an American doctor, was working in the DRC during an ongoing outbreak that has resulted in dozens of deaths. In response, US health officials have confirmed the case and announced "proactive measures" to protect the US public. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) have implemented enhanced travel screening, entry restrictions, and public health measures to prevent the spread of Ebola in the US. The overall risk to the American public and travelers remains low, according to health officials. The measures aim to prevent the Ebola virus disease from entering the United States amid ongoing outbreaks in East and Central Africa.

Ebola in Congo as CDC announces new travel screening measures Health officials to take ‘proactive measures’ in response to the ongoing Ebola virus epidemic in the DRC and Uganda
stories.summary: Somaliland has marked its first Independence Day following Israeli recognition. The move may have broader implications for the Middle East. Meanwhile, the US has announced that an American citizen has contracted Ebola in the Congo. In response to the ongoing Ebola virus epidemic in the DRC and Uganda, the CDC has announced new travel screening measures. Health officials will take proactive measures to address the situation. This development comes as Israel continues to expand its diplomatic relations, having formal ties with 168 countries as of 2021. The Israeli government has also confirmed a "Greater Israel" policy, aiming to advance its regional agenda amidst internal conflicts in neighboring countries. The US and other countries are closely monitoring the situation, with potential implications for regional stability and global health security.

stories.headline: Hezbollah War Persists Despite Truce Extension Air Defenses Activated in Isfahan for Unknown Reason, Iran's Mehr News Agency Reports. Trump Says He Called Off an Attack on Iran Scheduled for Tuesday at Gulf
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced he called off a planned attack on Iran, scheduled for Tuesday, at the request of Gulf leaders. This decision comes amid ongoing tensions between Iran and the US, as well as Israel. Recently, Iran's air defenses were activated in Isfahan for an unknown reason, according to Mehr News Agency. The region has seen increased military activity, with Iran launching attacks on Israeli and Gulf targets. Israel has also conducted attacks on Iranian sites, including the Natanz enrichment site, which was impacted according to the IAEA. A truce extension has been reported in the Hezbollah war, despite continued violence in Lebanon. The situation remains volatile, with multiple parties involved in the conflict and ongoing military operations in the region. Trump's decision to pause the planned attack may aim to de-escalate the situation.

stories.headline: Apple Sends Out WWDC 2026 Invites With A “Coming Bright Up” Tease
stories.summary: Apple has sent out invites for its WWDC 2026 event, which will take place from June 8 to June 12. The conference will kick off with a keynote at 10 a.m. PT/1 p.m. ET on June 8. This year's tagline is "Coming bright up," teasing upcoming announcements. The invites have been shared with members of the media, and the event is expected to feature significant updates and reveals from Apple. The WWDC 2026 keynote will likely showcase new software, technologies, and innovations from the company. With the "Coming bright up" tagline, Apple is generating buzz and anticipation for the event, which will be closely watched by tech enthusiasts and industry professionals. The five-day conference will provide a platform for Apple to unveil its latest developments and plans.

stories.headline: Peter G. Neumann, Who Warned of Computer Security Risks, Dies at 93
stories.summary: Peter G. Neumann, a prominent computer security researcher, died on May 17, 2026, at the age of 93, due to complications from a traumatic fall. Born on September 21, 1932, Neumann spent seven decades chronicling computer system failures and advocating for improved security and individual digital privacy. He was a vocal critic of the industry's lax attitudes toward computer security, developing solutions to enhance security and privacy in the digital realm. Neumann's work pioneered foundational concepts in modern computing, and his legacy continues to influence the field. A lifelong passion for music also defined him, often leading colleagues in Gilbert and Sullivan songs at conferences. His dedication to understanding complexity was inspired by a 1952 meeting with Albert Einstein, shaping his career as a critical voice in the industry. Neumann's contributions remain significant in the field of computer security.

stories.headline: Amazon launches Alexa Podcasts, an AI feature that generates full episodes from licensed news content
stories.summary: Amazon has launched Alexa Podcasts, a feature that uses AI to generate entire podcast episodes on demand. The feature, available to US Alexa+ customers, allows users to request a topic and then review an outline with options to set length or tone before approving production. The AI-generated episodes are narrated by two virtual co-hosts and can be created in minutes. The feature utilizes licensed journalism from over 200 newsrooms to generate podcast-style episodes on virtually any topic. The launch raises questions about the ethics, accuracy, and reliability of AI-generated content, particularly when covering news or complex topics. Alexa Podcasts is available for immediate listening, with no preparation or documents needed, and can be accessed wherever the user is. The feature is a significant development in AI-generated audio content.

stories.headline: Google I/O 2026: How to watch
stories.summary: Google I/O 2026 kicks off on May 19, with the entire two-day event livestreamed for free. Registration to watch is available at io.google/2026. The conference is expected to feature updates on Gemini AI, Android 17, and a preview of smart glasses. Keynotes will be livestreamed, providing updates on new features in Android, Chrome, AI, and more. The event will include two days of programming after the initial show. Google's annual developers conference will showcase the company's latest developments and innovations, with no ticket required to catch any of the livestreamed content. Viewers can watch the event live without leaving the designated window, with access to the full schedule and programming available online.

stories.headline: Antonio Rudiger stays! Real Madrid defender agrees to sign new contract Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger has agreed to a one-year contract extension at the Bernabeu despite interest from Saudi Arabia.
stories.summary: Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger has agreed to a one-year contract extension, committing to another season with the Spanish giants. Despite initial interest in a two-year extension for long-term security, Rudiger accepted the proposal. He had also received a lucrative offer from Saudi Arabia but chose to remain with Real Madrid, believing he can achieve more success with the club. Rudiger's current deal was set to expire at the end of the ongoing campaign, but he will now stay on for an additional year. The German centre-back's decision comes after considering alternatives, ultimately deciding to prioritize his time with Real Madrid over other opportunities. The contract renewal ensures Rudiger will continue to be a part of the team for the upcoming season.

stories.headline: IPL 2026 Playoffs Scenarios: 5 Teams, 1 Spot - Race To Top 4 Heats Up After CSK's Loss vs SRH The IPL 2026 race to the playoffs just got more intense for five teams, who will be fighting for just one spot
stories.summary: The IPL 2026 playoff race has intensified with five teams competing for one remaining spot. Sunrisers Hyderabad's five-wicket win over Chennai Super Kings has added to the competition. Currently, RCB, GT, and SRH are leading, while PBKS, RR, and CSK are still in contention. DC and KKR must win to stay in the race, while MI and LSG have been eliminated. The top four spots are still up for grabs, with eight teams initially in contention. The teams' chances of qualification are determined by their maximum possible points and net run rate (NRR) breakdown. The playoff scenarios are constantly updating as matches progress, with an interactive predictor available to simulate remaining matches and track qualification chances for all 10 teams.

stories.headline: Gov. Pritzker says Mayor Johnson has 'no plan' to keep the Bears in Chicago The governor’s remarks about the way the mayor does business with the Illinois General Assembly revive early tensions between the two men that they had seemingl
stories.summary: Governor J.B. Pritzker stated that Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson has 'no plan' to keep the Bears in Chicago. The governor's comments reignite early tensions between the two men, related to their working relationship with the Illinois General Assembly. Pritzker's remarks suggest a disagreement on how to approach business with the state legislature. The tension between Pritzker and Johnson has been ongoing, with the governor previously expressing opposition to the mayor's budget plan, including a proposed "head tax." The latest comments come as Johnson aims to keep the Bears in Chicago, with Pritzker questioning the effectiveness of the mayor's approach. The exchange highlights the ongoing dynamic between the governor and the mayor, with Pritzker's diplomatic tone giving way to criticism of Johnson's methods.

stories.headline: Conor McGregor’s planning application for Straffan home extension ‘deemed invalid’ Kildare County Council says drawings submitted were ‘misleading and incorrect’
stories.summary: Kildare County Council has deemed Conor McGregor's planning application for a home extension in Straffan as invalid. The council stated that the drawings submitted with the application were "misleading and incorrect". As a result, the application has been invalidated due to the inaccurate information provided. McGregor had submitted the application for an extension to his residence, but the council's decision has put the project on hold. The issue with the drawings and information submitted has led to the application being rejected, and it is unclear at this time whether McGregor will resubmit a revised application to address the council's concerns. The decision was made after a review of the application, highlighting the importance of accurate and complete information in the planning process.

stories.headline: CAA applicants must declare passport status and surrender foreign passports, per new Home Ministry guidelines following West Bengal elections.
stories.summary: The Indian Home Ministry has introduced new guidelines for Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) applicants. Applicants from Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh must declare their foreign passport status and surrender their passports within 15 days of citizenship approval. The new rules, known as the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, aim to simplify procedures for Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholders and citizenship applicants. Successful applicants will be required to relinquish their foreign passports, ensuring they hold only Indian citizenship. The guidelines come after the West Bengal elections and are part of the government's efforts to regulate citizenship and immigration processes. The rules apply to minority communities from the specified countries who have arrived in India.

stories.headline: Delhi recorded its hottest day of the season as temperatures crossed 44°C; IMD issued a yellow heatwave alert for Tue–Fri with highs near 45°C.
stories.summary: Delhi recorded its hottest day of the season with temperatures crossing 44°C. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow heatwave alert for Tuesday to Friday, warning of highs near 45°C. The weather office forecasted a mainly clear sky with heatwave conditions at isolated places. Temperatures are expected to remain harsh, with maximum temperatures likely touching 45°C in parts of the capital. The yellow alert cautions residents about excessive heat, rising heat stress, and hot dry winds through the week. The warning will stay intact until May 22. Residents are advised to take precautions due to the severe heatwave conditions. The IMD has warned that temperatures may reach 45°C this week, prompting the yellow alert for Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR).

stories.headline: The Court had reserved its verdict in January after hearing the final leg of submissions made by various States, the NHAI and the AWBI.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court reserved its verdict in January after hearing final submissions from various states, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), and the Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) regarding stray dog management. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta, and NV Anjaria heard the pleas seeking modification of earlier orders in the stray dogs case. The case was initiated by the Supreme Court last year to examine measures being taken to manage the stray dog population. The court will deliver its judgement on May 19. The verdict comes after the court heard submissions from various stakeholders, including states and the NHAI, on the issue of stray dog management and potential modifications to previous judicial orders. The judgement is expected to provide clarity on the management of stray dogs in India.

stories.headline: Judges Inquiry Committee submits report on Justice Yashwant Varma to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
stories.summary: The Judges Inquiry Committee has submitted its report to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla regarding allegations against Justice Yashwant Varma. The committee was formed on August 12, 2025, to investigate claims that cash was found at Justice Varma's official residence in Delhi after an accidental fire in March 2024. Justice Varma has denied these allegations. The report was submitted to Speaker Birla in Parliament House on Monday. The committee's findings have not been disclosed. The inquiry was initiated after allegations of corruption surfaced, prompting Speaker Birla to constitute a three-member committee to probe the matter. The submission of the report marks a significant development in the case, which will now likely proceed to the next stage of consideration by the Lok Sabha Speaker. The details of the report's contents and recommendations are not yet publicly known.

stories.headline: Norwegian PM flags "weaponisation" of trade Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre on Monday said that countries committed to a rule-based international order must 'move closer together' and strengthen
stories.summary: Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre called for closer ties between nations that uphold a rules-based international order, citing concerns over the "weaponisation" of trade, diplomacy, and critical supply chains. He emphasized the need for cooperation among countries committed to this order, as the global system is evolving. Støre made these comments at the Norway-India Business and Research Summit in Oslo, where he met with Indian Prime Minister Modi. He stressed the importance of a rules-based global order and cooperation over isolation to address global challenges. Støre's remarks come amid growing concerns about the use of trade and diplomacy as tools for geopolitical leverage, and the need for like-minded countries to work together to maintain a stable international order. He urged nations to move closer together and strengthen cooperation to counter these challenges.

stories.headline: Game Theory Says Taiwan May Be The World’s Most Dangerous Standoff Game theory is a helpful framework for understanding markets and geopolitics, and right now, there’s no better place to apply it than Taiwan
stories.summary: Tensions between the US and China over Taiwan have escalated, with Chinese leader Xi Jinping warning of an "extremely dangerous place" if the US ignores Chinese demands. Game theory suggests that the high cost of conflict may lead rational actors to cooperate. Taiwan's importance in the AI revolution and its deepening economic ties with the US could serve as a deterrent against catastrophe. The US has treaty obligations to Taiwan, while China has plans for invasion. The risk of nuclear escalation is a concern in a potential US-China conflict over Taiwan. The situation is complex, with the US and China weighing the costs and benefits of using force or seeking accommodation to determine Taiwan's future. The analysis explores the current tensions, invasion plans, and treaty obligations to assess the likelihood of war between the US and China over Taiwan.

stories.headline: Geopolitics has changed since last India-Nordic Summit, conflicts on agenda for talks: Norwegian envoy Norway seeks to increase energy supplies to India amid geopolitical discussions at the India-Nordic Summit, addressing conflicts and economic impact
stories.summary: The India-Nordic Summit is set to take place in Oslo on May 18th, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi attending alongside the heads of state of Sweden, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland. Norway's envoy stated that geopolitics has changed since the last summit, and conflicts will be on the agenda for talks. Norway seeks to increase energy supplies to India, particularly as US sanction waivers on Russian oil lapse. The summit will focus on energy, trade, and strategic ties, with over 20 MoUs expected to be signed across energy and technology sectors. Discussions will also cover trade, investments, and geopolitical issues, with India and the Nordic countries sharing a common interest in defending world order and stability. The summit marks India's third meeting with the Nordic nations, having previously met in Stockholm and Copenhagen.

stories.headline: Surging Bond Yields & Potential Warsh Fed Test Could Be Sword Of Damocles For Stocks (SPY) Stock market outlook: inflation, rising Treasury yields, and geopolitics raise correction risk despite AI strength
stories.summary: US Treasury yields are expected to remain high, with the 30-year bond yield surpassing 5%, a key psychological threshold. This surge, driven by hot inflation data and rising oil prices, may weigh on stocks. Incoming Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh faces a challenging outlook, with markets skeptical about his ability to tame inflation. The yield increase complicates Warsh's policy plans and reshapes Fed rate-cut odds. Geopolitics and inflation concerns also contribute to a higher correction risk for the stock market, despite strength in the AI sector. Investors are bracing for higher yields to persist, potentially impacting the stock market outlook, with the S&P 500 index (SPY) vulnerable to a correction. The combination of rising yields, inflation, and geopolitics creates uncertainty for the market.

stories.headline: Sensex Rises Over 300 Points, Nifty Crosses 23,700 Amid Positive Market Sentiment
stories.summary: The Indian stock market extended gains for the second consecutive session, with the Sensex rising over 300 points and the Nifty crossing 23,700. The BSE Sensex gained 330.23 points to trade at 75,645.27, while the NSE Nifty 50 traded at 23,759.65, up 347.05 points. Cooling bond yields, a slight drop in oil prices, and persistent foreign institutional investor (FII) buying boosted investor sentiment. IT stocks led the rally, with the Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices also seeing gains. The market's positive trend was also influenced by global market trends and optimism surrounding ongoing US-China talks. The previous day's gains, with the Sensex rising over 1,000 points, supported the current upward momentum, driven by value buying and easing volatility. The overall market sentiment remained positive, with investors showing optimism about the market's future performance.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Closing Bell | Sensex, Nifty 50 End Flat On May 18; IT Stocks Rebound, Rupee Hits Record Low Amid Rising Crude Oil Prices
stories.summary: The Indian stock market closed flat on May 18, with the Sensex falling 46 points and the Nifty 50 ending near 24,334. The market opened sharply lower due to surging oil prices, but IT stocks rebounded later in the day. The rupee hit a record low amid rising crude oil prices. Despite the initial downturn, the Nifty 50 recovered 100 points from its day's low. The top stock gainers were in the tech sector, leading the market's gains. The Bank Nifty and BSE Sensex also experienced fluctuations, with analysts providing detailed analysis, support, and resistance levels for the indices. Overall, the market ended with a modest downside, influenced by global economic factors and crude oil price increases.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex ends over 1,100 points higher from day's low; Nifty 50 near 23,650
stories.summary: The Sensex and Nifty 50 indices ended in the green on Monday, with the Sensex rising 77 points to 75,315 and the Nifty 50 edging up 6 points to 23,649. The indices staged a sharp rebound from the day's lows, with the Sensex recovering over 1,100 points from its intraday low of 74,180. The recovery was driven by value buying in select heavyweights. Prior to the rebound, the Sensex had tumbled 1,134.78 points, or 1.50%, and the Nifty had fallen 3.5% and 4% respectively over the last six sessions. The indices ended near the flatline, with the Sensex up 0.10% and the Nifty up 0.03%. The recovery helped mitigate some of the losses, but broader markets remained under pressure. The Sensex and Nifty's rebound was a significant turnaround from their earlier losses.

stories.headline: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
stories.summary: Stock market action on Tuesday will be influenced by several factors. On Monday, the US markets extended losses, with the Nasdaq leading declines due to pressure on semiconductor shares. Surging Treasury yields and oil prices also raised concerns about inflation and borrowing costs. In contrast, European markets traded with gains, with most major indices showing advances. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was up 0.53% to 26,086.10. On the BSE, 3,087 stocks declined, 1,162 advanced, and 162 remained unchanged. The overall market sentiment was bearish in the US, but bullish in Europe. These global market trends, along with other factors, will shape the stock market action on Tuesday. The number of declining stocks outnumbered advancing stocks on the BSE, indicating a negative trend.

stories.headline: Elon Musk Loses Blockbuster OpenAI Suit
stories.summary: A US jury found OpenAI not liable in a lawsuit brought by Elon Musk, who claimed the organization's CEO, Sam Altman, and others had unlawfully enriched themselves. The jury ruled that Musk waited too long to bring the lawsuit, barring his claims due to statutes of limitations. The lawsuit targeted Altman, President Greg Brockman, the OpenAI Foundation, and Microsoft. Musk's legal team plans to appeal the decision. Microsoft welcomed the jury's decision, stating that the facts and timeline in the case were clear. The verdict was announced in Oakland federal court, with OpenAI's attorney appearing pleased, while Musk's team seemed disappointed. The case centered on Musk's allegations that OpenAI had strayed from its original mission to benefit humanity, but the jury's decision effectively dismissed his claims.

stories.headline: Elon Musk loses lawsuit against Open AI and its top executives
stories.summary: A California jury has ruled in favor of OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in a lawsuit filed by Elon Musk. The jury found that Musk waited too long to bring the lawsuit, which was barred by the statute of limitations. The verdict was unanimous and came after approximately 90 minutes of deliberation. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed with the jury's decision. Musk had alleged that OpenAI strayed from its original mission to benefit humanity, but the jury's ruling means the company is not liable. Musk has stated that he will appeal the decision, calling it a "calendar technicality" in a post on X. The lawsuit was a high-profile showdown between Musk and Altman, with the jury's verdict marking a significant defeat for the Tesla chief. Musk plans to appeal the decision.

stories.headline: While Trump insisted the Iran war would end ‘soon,’ an account in his name was 'Selling America'
stories.summary: A brokerage account in President Trump's name made 3,642 trades in the first quarter of 2026, hedging against a war with Iran. This contradicts Trump's public statements that the war is nearly won and will end "soon." Trump has repeatedly changed his timeline for ending the conflict, while escalating threats against Iran. He claims a major goal of the war is to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and that Iran's leadership wants a deal. However, his defense secretary has stated that the war is "just the beginning." The discrepancy between Trump's public statements and his financial transactions has raised questions about his true intentions and the potential outcome of the conflict. Trump's inconsistent messaging has led to confusion and skepticism about his ability to end the war "very soon" as he claims.

stories.headline: Harry Crosbie sues over proposed Vicar Street Hotel
stories.summary: Businessman Harry Crosbie has initiated Commercial Court proceedings against a hotel company over the proposed Vicar Street Hotel in Dublin. The hotel is planned at the Thomas Street location of Vicar Street, a concert and events venue owned by Crosbie and operated by Peter Aiken. The venue has a capacity of 1,050 people for seated performances and 1,500 people for standing gigs. Crosbie's dispute with the hotel company has led to the Commercial Court proceedings, although specific details of the dispute have not been disclosed. The case is ongoing, with Crosbie seeking resolution through the court. The proposed hotel development has sparked the legal action, with Crosbie contesting the plans for the Vicar Street Hotel at his events venue.

stories.headline: Federal court rejects Elon Musk's claims against Open AI, saying he filed his lawsuit too late OAKLAND, California — A federal court on Monday dismissed claims filed against OpenAI and its top executives by Elon Musk, who accused them of betraying a share
stories.summary: A federal court in Oakland, California, dismissed Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and its top executives, including CEO Sam Altman. Musk had accused them of betraying a shared vision for the company. The court ruled that Musk filed his lawsuit too late, waiting too long to sue OpenAI and its CEO. Musk's lawsuit, which sought $150 billion in damages, was rejected by the federal jury. The decision potentially brings an end to the court fight between Musk and OpenAI. Musk expressed his thoughts on the decision in a post on X, following the jury's ruling on Monday. The dismissal of the claims marks a significant development in the high-profile case, which centered on allegations of a breached shared vision for OpenAI.

stories.headline: Federal court rejects Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI, saying he filed his lawsuit too late A federal court on Monday dismissed claims filed against OpenAI and its top executives by Elon Musk, who accused them of betraying a shared vision for it to rem
stories.summary: A federal court dismissed Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and its top executives, citing that he filed his lawsuit too late. Musk accused OpenAI of betraying a shared vision to remain a nonprofit dedicated to guiding artificial intelligence's development for humanity's benefit. His lawsuit claimed breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment by OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman and others. Musk also made antitrust claims against OpenAI and Microsoft, but the judge expressed skepticism due to aggressive competition in the AI market. The court's decision was unanimous, with the jury rejecting Musk's claims. The lawsuit's dismissal marks a significant development in the dispute between Musk and OpenAI, with the court ultimately ruling that Musk's delayed filing was the reason for the dismissal.

stories.headline: Federal court rejects Elon Musk’s claims against OpenAI, saying he filed his lawsuit too late A federal court on Monday dismissed claims filed against OpenAI and its top executives by Elon Musk, who accused them of betraying a shared vision for it to gui
stories.summary: A federal court in Oakland, California, has dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and its top executives, including CEO Sam Altman. Musk had accused them of betraying a shared vision for OpenAI to develop artificial intelligence as a nonprofit dedicated to humanity's benefit. He claimed breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment, alleging that Altman and others profited from OpenAI's soaring valuation. The court rejected Musk's claims, citing that he filed the lawsuit too late. A federal jury unanimously agreed with the decision. Musk also made antitrust claims against OpenAI and Microsoft, but the judge has not yet ruled on those claims, having previously expressed skepticism due to the competitive nature of the AI market. The dismissal marks a significant setback for Musk's legal efforts against OpenAI.

stories.headline: Jury rules against Elon Musk A U.S. jury on Monday ruled against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI, finding the artificial intelligence company not liable to the world’s richest perso
stories.summary: A US jury ruled against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI, finding the company not liable. Musk had claimed OpenAI prioritized commercial gain over the public good and strayed from its original mission of developing AI for humanity's benefit. OpenAI denied the allegations. The jury decided Musk's claims were barred by the statute of limitations, meaning he brought the case too late. The verdict was unanimous, delivered after less than two hours of deliberation in a federal courthouse in Oakland, California. The lawsuit was filed by Musk, who is the world's richest person, against the artificial intelligence company he had previously been involved with. The jury's decision brings an end to the lawsuit, with OpenAI not being held liable to Musk.
